newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trygg-Hansa says to sell reinsurer to Focus, Medway.
newsitem.headline: Trygg-Hansa says to sell reinsurer to Focus, Medway.

text.p: Swedish insurer Trygg-Hansa AB said on Wednesday it intended to sell its reinsurance operations in the U.S. and Canada to the Canadian run-off firm Focus Group.
Focus will in turn sell half of the operations to Britain's Medway Insurance Group.
"Focus Group will split the operations into one ongoing business and one run-off part," Jan Bruneheim, head of Trygg-Hansa's Run off unit, told Reuters.
"Focus will take the run-off part and phase it out, while Britain's Medway Insurance Group Plc will buy the ongoing business (Hansa Re)".
Medway on Wednesday issued a statement saying it intends to seek admission to London's Alternative Investment Market (AIM) by way of a private placement of 70 million pounds sterling, Bruneheim said.
Medway was founded in December 1996 as a Lloyd's orientated U.S. licensed insurance company.
Earlier on Wednesday, Trygg-Hansa said it signed a preliminary agreement with an international group of investors to sell the operations in question, but did not name the buyer.
The deal is conditioned on Medway's private placement as well as approval by U.S. and Canadian authorities, the company said.
"The deal is a natural step in the phasing out of received reinsurance and means, if it is finalised, that insurance technical debt is reduced by about 350 million crowns," the company said.
Trygg-Hansa has issued limited guarantees during a period of five years for its previous insurance responsibility.
The deal will free-up $60 million in cash and will generate a small capital gain, the company said.
